points.name: CREtech and MetaProp track the proptech market

points.name: BOMA covers commercial building operations

points.name: NAR REACH backs the startups

points.desc: The residential brokerage's platform applies AI to agent workflows, client matching, and predictive listing recommendations.
points.name: Compass runs AI inside the brokerage workflow

points.desc: HouseCanary's valuation and forecasting models and Cherre's data integration layer are what institutional investors underwrite on - the wholesale side of the AVM story.
points.name: Institutional valuation runs on data platforms

points.name: Smart buildings close the operations loop

summary: Automated valuation is the sector's oldest deployed AI, and it is now formally regulated: federal quality-control standards for AVMs took effect in 2025. Valuation, leasing automation, 3D capture, and property operations are where AI actually runs; the regulator record and the platforms' own model documentation are the sources.

analysis.body:
# Real Estate

According to the Census Bureau, 28.9 percent of firms in real estate and rental and leasing reported using AI in the two weeks prior to their survey response, up from 28.0 percent in the prior period. That steady adoption reflects a sector where AI has moved from experimental to operational across three distinct layers: valuation, property operations, and transaction workflow.

Automated valuation models are the sector's oldest and most consequential AI application. Zillow publishes Zestimates for over 110 million homes using neural network-based models that incorporate county records, MLS data, and hundreds of data points per property, with updates multiple times per week. Opendoor and other iBuyers rely on proprietary pricing models to make immediate purchase offers, exposing their balance sheets directly to model accuracy. HouseCanary serves institutional investors with AI-powered valuations, forecasts, and analytics across 136 million U.S. properties. Recognizing the systemic importance of these models in mortgage underwriting, the FHFA, CFPB, OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC, and NCUA jointly adopted a final rule implementing quality control standards for automated valuation models used by mortgage originators and secondary market issuers. That rule requires institutions to adopt policies and control systems ensuring AVMs meet quality standards, protect against data manipulation, avoid conflicts of interest, and undergo random sample testing and reviews. This represents the first binding federal regulation of AI in the industry.

Commercial real estate operations concentrate AI in property management and leasing automation. JLL states it has invested more in AI technology than any other real estate company and deploys it across brokerage, facilities, and portfolio analytics. Building Engines' Prism platform is an AI-powered property management system that delivers instant recommendations and automation to help teams cut costs and grow net operating income. EliseAI provides agentic conversational AI for housing and property management, handling messages, calls, and task automation around the clock, including tour scheduling, lead follow-up, and maintenance requests integrated with existing systems. Prophia extracts lease terms, rent rolls, and obligations from commercial lease documents using AI combined with expert validation to create structured, verified lease data for owners and operators.

On the residential brokerage and advisory side, Compass applies AI to agent workflows and client matching, while the National Association of Realtors tracks technology adoption across its membership and operates REACH, an accelerator for proptech scale-ups created by Second Century Ventures, positioned as the most active venture fund in global real estate technology. Matterport captures buildings as 3D data using cameras and software, automatically generating virtual tours and floor plans, and integrating with platforms like Procore and Autodesk to centralize portfolio management, reduce site visits, and improve ROI. The Building Owners and Managers Association provides resources and advocacy for professionals managing commercial properties across all asset classes, staying current on smart-building trends and operations innovation.

Regulatory scrutiny is narrowing to model transparency and consumer protection. The CFPB and FHFA's AVM quality control rule mandates that institutions applying valuation models in credit decisions and securitization maintain documented procedures ensuring high confidence in estimates, protection against manipulation, and avoidance of conflicts of interest. For firms considering AI deployment in real estate, the pattern is clear: valuation models must now meet federal standards; property operations yield measurable cost and efficiency gains; and adoption is already material across the sector, suggesting that integration into core workflows rather than pilot projects has become the baseline expectation.
